![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14219884/assets/01aba7550fb134b1f3a93276dc8f3b91794844ea21254c2c75a0702a443a60e3.png)

Which of the diagrams above shows three collinear points?
question.worked_solution:
Three (or more) points are collinear if a straight line passes through all points.

With that in mind, let's examine our diagrams in turn.

- Diagram I shows three collinear points. There is a straight line that passes through all three of these points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14219884/assets/6310ff39996be529bc44e5058ef9710400f0c8089196a57e7f4eb541703e53ae.png)

- Diagram II shows three points that are *not* collinear. We can't draw a straight line that passes through all three points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14219884/assets/6334d2bc1fda6390b6ec542afb8cc37d4f76322b98d41ca6bbb3af3c8d735c8f.png)

- Diagram III shows three points that are *not* collinear. We can't draw a straight line that passes through all three points.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14219884/assets/8939cff2d7cc8ca9a08c7be63517ffb900e49b769edc5c2454119f4da25904cc.png)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
